items.title: Tom Albert Interview, 1962-05-07
items.q: Chris Kelly got the cornet book and he died, and I never did got it the most.

ctx.x: Did you ever hear of Scott Joplin? Scott Joplin? He was, it wasn't from here, but he wrote music.

Oh, these are them Scott Joplin books, them red books? Yeah. Well I bought four of them. Yeah? Chris Kelly got the cornet book and he died, and I never did got it the most. Yeah, did you? I wrote it to him, I never did got my cornet. I got the violin part down in the locker there somewhere. Yeah, the violin part. But in them parts they had no saxophone then, you understand? Well they had the trombone part, the violin, cornet, I bought four books. The only four of them I see was trombone, trombone, violin, clarinet.
Well what did Chris Kelly play? The cornet.

items.title: Tom Albert Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: Sam Morgan, all of them little bands, Rene, Chris Kelly, all of them little bands, all of them little bands, all of them little bands come to me.

ctx.x: A parlor. They called me a parlor. They used to call me a parlor music. But after a while all of them would come by the parlor music. Yeah. Yeah, a musician. They used to call me a parlor musician because I used to play all the music, you understand? And like the piano and the thing, you put the coffee up there and play it. You see, that one used to call me a parlor musician. Yeah. But when they come to parlor, when they had to read, they all of them come to me. Every one of them, every one of them come to me.…
It's by the… Yeah. The music. The count of the lives.

items.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21
items.q: And Chris Kelly, I had them all come here to want music then.

ctx.x: Yeah. He was, his time and the division and all that.

Yeah. He noticed all, but he couldn't, he wasn't sure he could count, you know. Yeah. The division, you know. He didn't show he could count. He, he come out and eat with me. I've been him playing it about four times. Yeah. And I told him, I said, you can go. But after he played, I know some of them fellas, you put them in them shop keys and four and five flats, they- Yeah. They could read it all right. Some of them, they couldn't read it, you understand. They had routine, I played all right. But they used to call…

I used to have some better. I was going to ask some more about the trombone, the two brothers, Yank and Buddy. Which was the better trombone, do you think, Mooney? Which would you rather hear? If you had your choice to hear, was one of them better than the other? I was about to say.
